newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: First Iraqi food imports to total $70m - U.N. envoy.
newsitem.headline: First Iraqi food imports to total $70m - U.N. envoy.

text.p: The first food contracts under the United Nations-Iraq "oil-for-food" scheme were formally approved on Thursday, allowing the importation of a total of $70 million worth of wheat and rice, according to Portuguese ambassador Antonio Monteiro, chairman of the U.N.'s sanction's committee on Iraq.
"This is very good, very positive as all of this is working," said Monteiro.
The scheme, which took effect on December 10, allows Iraq to sell up to $2 billion of oil as an exception to broad sanctions in place since the 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
About two-thirds of the proceeds can be used, under strict U.N. supervision, to purchase food and other humanitarian goods with the rest going for war reparations and other costs.
Monteiro said the grain is expected to arrive in Iraq in about a month.

The wheat, which will be for slightly above $50.50 million -- around 250,000 tonnes -- will be sent from Australia. The rice, for $21.3 million -- about 60,000 tonnes -- will come from Thailand, U.N. officials said.

Some diplomats erroneously reported after the sanctions committee that the rice contract was for $5 million. There is a pending contract for $5 million of detergent which is expected to be approved next week.

Monteiro said the committee decided Thursday to turn down a request to allow Iraq to import technology to improve agricultural yields as that was more of a long-term project and fell outside the humanitarian purpose of the scheme.
